transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-14
Start: 16:30 EDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ben Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood CSM); Lisa Morgan (Aurora Security Lead), Tom Reyes (Aurora IT Ops), Naveen Patel (Aurora Compliance), Ellen Wu (Eng Lead)

[00:00] Ben Carter: hey everyone thanks for joining, we know schedules tight so we'll jump in. this is the SOC2 and ISO posture review for Aurora Financial. i'm ben carter from redwood, with priya our SE, maya from success.
[00:18] Lisa Morgan: thanks, appreciate it. we mainly want assurance around reports, mappings, and how your trust center works. also specifics on audit logs and KMS key ownership.
[00:30] Priya Shah: great, the plan is quick overview of artifacts we can share, then run through SSO/RBAC, audit logs, data residency, encryption and private deployment options. we'll leave time at the end for Q&A and next steps.
[01:05] Tom Reyes: one quick ask, we need to know if keys can be customer-managed in KMS for private or dedicated deployments. our compliance team insists on customer key control for some workflows.
[01:22] Priya Shah: yes, for Redwood Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations; for Hosted API we encrypt at rest with our keys but offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise contracts. i'll clarify the exact supported providers in the follow-up.
[01:55] Lisa Morgan: and SOC 2? we need the latest Type II report, plus the ISO 27001 cert, and ideally a mapping of Redwood controls to our control framework.
[02:10] Ben Carter: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate through our Trust Center. i'll upload the redacted report and metadata link after this call. link is in the deck but i'll inbox you — trust center: https://trust.redwood.ai (note: placeholder link).
[02:40] Naveen Patel: do you provide a control mapping file? like a spreadsheet mapping SOC 2 CC controls to ISO or to specific controls we can reference in our audits?
[02:55] Priya Shah: yes, we commonly run a controls mapping workshop. priya: we prepare a template that maps SOC 2 and ISO controls to Redwood policies and evidence types — we'll show an example in the workshop and attach the template to the Trust Center.
[03:22] Ellen Wu: curious about audit logs retention and whether we can stream logs to our SIEM. we need 1 year retention and near-real-time forwarding.
[03:38] Samir Khan (Redwood): we provide audit logs for admin actions, tenant events, and API access. retention depends on plan; Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer retention and push logs to your logging endpoint via syslog/HTTPS or cloud storage. hosted has default retention but we can arrange longer retention as an add-on.
[04:05] Lisa Morgan: does the audit log include content-level data or just metadata? we can't have customer PII in logs.
[04:20] Priya Shah: logs are metadata by default — request IDs, timestamps, user IDs, API key IDs, IPs, model and route. content is not included in standard audit logs. for debug traces we have a separate process and require redaction/consent; for enterprise we can set processes to avoid capturing PII. sometimes transcribed as "we don't log content by defaut" in notes.
[04:55] Tom Reyes: about SSO, we use SAML SSO with SCIM for provisioning. how mature is your SSO integration and RBAC model?
[05:10] Ben Carter: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning in Enterprise. RBAC is role-based with admin/engineer/audit roles; you can create custom roles and map SAML assertions to roles. Priya will share the SSO implementation guide.
[05:40] Lisa Morgan: is there MFA enforced for admin accounts?
[05:48] Maya Lopez: yes we enforce MFA for admin-level access and recommend it for all users. for dedicated/private there are options to integrate with your org's MFA provider via SAML and conditional access.
[06:05] [short cross talk] Ben Carter: i'll also note we have SOC 2 controls around change management and deployment pipelines, we can provide evidence like change logs and control narrative.
[06:30] Naveen Patel: about penetration testing and vulnerability scans — do you do annual third-party pentests?
[06:42] Priya Shah: yes, annual third-party pentests and continuous vuln scanning; we share summary reports in Trust Center, with redacted findings for external consumption. full reports are available under NDA for customers in scope.
[07:12] Tom Reyes: network isolation — if we go dedicated or private, can we run in our VPC? we might need to keep traffic internal.
[07:25] Samir Khan: Private supports deployment into customer VPCs or on-prem packages for air-gapped environments for high-regulated customers. Dedicated is isolated within Redwood's infra but we provide private endpoints and VPC peering options. we'll document the network topologies.
[08:00] Lisa Morgan: data residency — we require EU residency for certain datasets, how do you guarantee region residency?
[08:12] Priya Shah: we allow region pinning; hosted models can be pinned to region endpoints and Dedicated/Private naturally run in chosen cloud regions or on-prem. we keep customer data in-region for pinning use cases and can provide attestations.
[08:40] Ellen Wu: curious about model fallbacks and caching — if we have sensitive prompts, do you cache the prompt plain text anywhere?
[08:52] Priya Shah: by default we cache model KV prefixes to reduce cost but we can disable caching for sensitive workloads; for private deployments the cache stays within your environment. we'll include config knobs in the controls mapping doc. also a note: sometimes "KV cache" is transcribed as "K-V cash" in our transcripts.
[09:30] Ben Carter: switching to encryption — at rest encryption uses AES-256, in transit TLS 1.2+; we support BYOK for Private and select enterprise agreements for Hosted. Key rotation policies are documented.
[09:55] Lisa Morgan: for BYOK do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault?
[10:05] Priya Shah: yes, we support major cloud KMS providers; HSM integration is possible for high-compliance customers. we'll include exact supported versions in the follow-up.
[10:30] Naveen Patel: evidence for key management — do you provide KMS audit logs or proof of key usage?
[10:40] Samir Khan: we can provide KMS usage metadata and attestations; for customer-owned keys the cloud provider's audit logs are the source of truth, but Redwood can correlate and provide mapping evidence.
[11:05] Lisa Morgan: procurement will want to see indemnity and data processing addendum — is DPA standard?
[11:15] Ben Carter: yes, we have a DPA and standard security addenda; legal can share redacted templates. procurement/legal topics usually follow after SOC/ISO docs.
[11:35] Tom Reyes: any limitations on on-prem package for the inference runtime? we need to know what versions of models are supported and how often security patches are released.
[11:50] Priya Shah: Private on-prem includes the runtime with a supported set of models; we publish a compatibility matrix and patch cadence. for mission-critical customers we can agree an SLA for patch windows.
[12:20] Lisa Morgan: could you summarize what you'll provide after this call?
[12:30] Ben Carter: yes — SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and ISO 27001 cert in Trust Center; controls mapping template and sample; SSO/SCIM and RBAC implementation guide; audit log capabilities and how to configure retention and forwarding; notes on BYOK/KMS and private deployment options; we'll also schedule a controls mapping workshop.
[12:55] Naveen Patel: perfect. one more nuance — do you have a list of sub-processors and data flow diagrams? we need that for our supply chain review.
[13:08] Maya Lopez: yes we publish sub-processor list and high-level data flow diagrams in Trust Center; detailed diagrams can be shared under NDA if needed.
[13:35] Ellen Wu: any performance implications if we disable caching or KV cache? we have low-latency SLAs for some paths.
[13:48] Priya Shah: disabling cache increases token cost and latency; for low-latency requirements we suggest Dedicated or Private with local KV caches. we can model latency impact with a short benchmark run during the POC.
[14:20] Tom Reyes: about PII redaction — do you offer automatic redaction options before logs or traces leave our environment?
[14:32] Samir Khan: yes, we have configurable redaction pipelines and pre-send hooks for private/dedicated so traces don't include PII. hosted also supports redaction rules but more limited.
[15:05] Ben Carter: let's capture next steps — i'll upload artifacts, priya will set up the controls mapping session, tom will prepare SSO metadata.
[15:18] Lisa Morgan: thanks everyone. we'll aim to get the security questionnaire back in a week or so.
[15:30] [wrap up] Ben Carter: thank you all — expect the Trust Center link and SOC2 artifacts by Monday 2025-08-18 and we'll send calendar invite for the workshop.
[15:50] [end of meeting] Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings and misspellings; proper nouns may be slightly off. "Redwood Dedicated" sometimes transcribed as "Redwood dedicated" or "RedWood Dedicated."
